note: Config Ignore Readonly is a single-hook bridge: config_ignore_readonly_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns() returns ConfigIgnoreConfig::fromConfig(config('config_ignore.settings'))->getFormated('simple'), i.e. the flat import/update ignore list at config_ignore.settings:ignored_config_entities (simple mode). config_readonly treats those patterns as editable-under-readonly. No UI/settings/permissions/schema/plugins. Medium cases seed config_ignore.settings:ignored_config_entities with a known value and the agent reads it back via drush cget. Hard cases clear that list (verify FAILS because the module then forwards no matching pattern -- note the alter hook still injects unrelated ai_provider_amazeeio patterns, so verify checks specifically for system.site / a glob matching system.rss) then the agent adds the pattern and verify confirms the module forwards it via the invoked hook. Baseline ignored_config_entities is empty; cleanup/reset restore [].

evals.prompt: The Drupal module config_ignore_readonly lets some config forms stay editable even when config_readonly has locked the site. Which Drupal hook does it implement, and how does it decide which forms remain editable?
evals.expected_output: It implements hook_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns(). It reads Config Ignore's ignore list (config_ignore.settings:ignored_config_entities, the simple import/update patterns via ConfigIgnoreConfig::getFormated('simple')) and returns those patterns to config_readonly as its whitelist, so any config form whose config is ignored stays editable while readonly is active.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with config_readonly active, I want the Basic site settings form (which edits system.site) to remain editable while config_ignore_readonly is enabled. What do I actually change to make that happen?
evals.expected_output: Add system.site to Config Ignore's ignore list (config_ignore.settings:ignored_config_entities). Because config_ignore_readonly forwards the ignore list to config_readonly's whitelist, ignoring system.site makes the site information form submittable even under readonly. No config_ignore_readonly-specific setting exists.

evals.prompt: Which Config Ignore pattern styles does config_ignore_readonly NOT support when deciding which forms stay editable under config_readonly?
evals.expected_output: Force-import patterns like ~webform.webform.contact are not supported, and partial/sub-key patterns like user.mail:register_no_approval_required.body are not supported (the whole config name must be ignored). Also, a form with multiple getEditableConfigNames() only becomes editable when all of them are ignored.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, Config Ignore is configured so that exactly one configuration object stays editable under config_readonly (via config_ignore_readonly). Inspect the live configuration and name that configuration object.
evals.expected_output: system.site: config_ignore.settings:ignored_config_entities is [system.site], and config_ignore_readonly forwards that to config_readonly's whitelist, so the Basic site settings form stays editable under readonly.

evals.prompt: This site uses config_ignore_readonly. Inspect Config Ignore's live settings and state which single configuration entity is currently ignored (and therefore has its form editable while config_readonly is active).
evals.expected_output: contact.form.feedback: it is the only entry in config_ignore.settings:ignored_config_entities, so config_ignore_readonly whitelists that config for editing under readonly.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site config_ignore_readonly, config_ignore and config_readonly are all enabled. Make the Basic site settings configuration (system.site) editable under config_readonly by configuring Config Ignore appropriately, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add system.site to config_ignore.settings:ignored_config_entities (simple mode). Then config_ignore_readonly_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns() returns a list containing system.site, so config_readonly leaves that form editable.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, make the system.rss configuration (and ideally all system.* configuration) remain editable while config_readonly is active, using config_ignore_readonly's mechanism. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add a pattern that matches system.rss -- either system.rss or the glob system.* -- to config_ignore.settings:ignored_config_entities. config_ignore_readonly forwards it to config_readonly's whitelist, so the matching config form(s) stay editable under readonly.
